submitter: bugs_open/477 lane. The second and last caller adopts delivery.Fill, which the bugs_open/475 lane landed at a026ed53b (council APPROVED, c8ed56d2). Their round was REVISEd, gated HIGH by the guardian, precisely for converting THIS file — so this conversion is mine to make and this is it.
rationale:
THE LAST HAND-KEPT MIRROR GOES, AND WITH IT THE TRAP I FILED A LANDMINE ABOUT THIS MORNING.

Until now two senders shared one filler (fillTemplate) and each carried its OWN hand-copied list of which placeholders it could produce. The second list was not derived from the first, so adding a token to the vocabulary silently disarmed the follow-up's guard: the token would be replaced by an EMPTY STRING, the post-fill '{{' scan would find nothing wrong BECAUSE THE FILL SUCCEEDED, and the only witness would be a customer reading 'The instructions are here: ' with nothing after it. I filed that as a LANDMINE (d67f08ff4) with the cross-reference at fillTemplate itself. This change makes the trap not exist, so the same commit DELETES the landmine — a warning about a fixed problem spends the next reader's attention on nothing. That deletion from a fleet-wide append-only ledger is deliberate and is stated in the commit message.

WHAT ACTUALLY BINDS ME NOW, PROVEN BY MUTATION RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Adding a token to delivery.Vocabulary and NOT declaring it here makes a live dispatch refuse pre-claim: 'this sender does not declare {{mutant}} … Nothing was stamped'. Removing FromClaim from my confirm-link declaration also fails. Both restored, green. That is the difference between a derivation and a second copy, and it is the only evidence worth having — the previous arrangement also compiled and also passed its tests.

THE ORDERING PROPERTY IS MINE TO ASSERT, NOT THE VOCABULARY'S, and this is the requirement I gave the 475 lane in their round. The two senders have DIFFERENT irreversible statements: delivery.Claim at send_delivery_email_action.go:154, ClaimFollowup at send_followup_email_action.go:188. A Check that ran after MY claim would pass every assertion in the shared helper while having already burnt followup_sent_at — the customer's single follow-up, spent on a refusal. So Check sits before ClaimFollowup and this package's own test asserts it with sqlmock given NO expectations, so any database touch fails.

FromClaim IS THE HALF THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A BLANK, and I am copying it because the council found it in their round, not because I spotted it. {{confirm_link}} is legitimately empty when Check runs — this sender mints its own token AFTER ClaimFollowup, where the delivery sender's is minted inside Claim. Same token, different provenance, which is exactly the per-caller-provenance point that made their first design unbuildable for me. Check exempts it; Apply then REFUSES if Claimed never supplied it. Without that second half the exemption is a hole straight to a customer's letter.

AND THE POST-FILL '{{' SCAN STAYS, though Check now makes it near-unreachable. Coverage asks whether the vocabulary KNOWS a token; the scan asks whether Apply actually SUBSTITUTED one. A declared token that Apply somehow failed to replace is invisible to Check by construction. I have written that distinction into the code at the scan, because after this change it looks redundant and it is not.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. No behaviour changes for any live dispatch: nothing calls this action yet (774/775 are deliberately unapplied — sites.followup_sent_at does not exist, there is no agent row and no schedule row). This is a refactor of an inert path onto a shared mechanism, and its value is that the NEXT placeholder cannot silently break it.

plan.summary: Convert the follow-up sender — the second and last caller — from a hand-kept placeholder mirror to a derived delivery.Fill, keeping the {{zip_link}} never-reason and the pre-ClaimFollowup ordering; then delete the now-callerless fillTemplate and the landmine whose trap no longer exists.

edits.symbol: SendFollowupEmailAction — the mirrored guard slice, the pre-substitution, the fill
edits.rationale: The declaration IS the guard. {{zip_link}} keeps its NeverReason verbatim ('a scheduled follow-up has no zip step and no presign to mint') because flattening it to 'empty => refuse' behaves identically today and loses the sentence that stops a later session wiring a presign into a scheduled sender. {{confirm_link}} is marked FromClaim and filled via Claimed after the mint. The {{instructions_link}} strings.ReplaceAll pre-substitution goes, so both letters now resolve that token through one vocabulary.

The refusal text moved (it now comes from the vocabulary and is better — it names the never-reason). The test's PROPERTIES are unchanged and one is added: the {{zip_link}} case now pins the never-reason sentence itself. A refusal that only says 'empty' invites a later session to 'fix' it by wiring a presign into a scheduled sender; pinning the sentence makes that a test failure rather than a plausible improvement. The still-claimable assertion is widened to accept either wording rather than the one literal, because an operator reading a scheduled refusal as a LOST follow-up will 'recover' it by hand.

Callerless after this conversion — verified by grep, not assumed. The 475 lane marked it deprecated-and-frozen and explicitly left its deletion to this commit, since removing it while my caller still used it would have been the concurrent-edit collision their own round was REVISEd for. stringOr STAYS: their converted caller still uses it four times.

A DELIBERATE deletion from a fleet-wide append-only ledger, stated as such because the pre-commit check will flag it and should. The entry warned that two guard lists had to be kept in step by hand. After this commit there is one derivation and no mirror, so the trap does not exist — and a landmine describing a fixed problem is worse than none, because it spends the next reader's attention on nothing. It is deleted only now, in the commit that makes it false: the 475 lane pulled their own deletion edit when their conversion of this file was refused, on the grounds that removing a warning from a still-live trap is worse than leaving a stale one. That reasoning is why the entry survived the intervening hours.
